title: **Proteome-wide analysis of cysteine oxidation using Stable Isotope Cysteine Labelling with Iodoacetamide \(SICyLIA)**
protocol: Plate cells to be compared in 10 cm dishes in regular medium and grow overnight at 37 °C with 5% CO₂.
Pre-chill bench top centrifuge to 4 °C.
Prepare lysis buffer 1 \(100 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 4% SDS) and immediately before cell lysis and protein extraction, add light or heavy iodoacetamide \(IAM) to achieve 55 mM IAM solutions.
Remove medium from cells and wash cell monolayers twice with pre-chilled PBS at 4 °C, ensuring thorough aspiration of PBS.
Add 500 µl of lysis buffer 1 with IAM per dish and immediately scrape cells using a cell lifter.
Collect lysates in Eppendorf tubes.
Sonicate lysates for 4 x 5 seconds to shear DNA/RNA.
Pre-chill plastic or glass dishes, scalpel, and forceps on dry ice.
Pre-chill Precellys24 bead-based homogeniser.
Prepare lysis buffer 1 and immediately before tissue homogenisation, add light or heavy IAM to achieve 55 mM IAM solutions.
Prepare homogenisation tubes by adding 800 µl lysis buffer with IAM.
Sacrifice mice by cervical dislocation.
Excise kidneys, place in plastic tubes, and snap freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen.
Once frozen, place kidneys on pre-chilled plastic or glass dishes on dry ice and excise representative samples.
Add frozen tissue slices to homogenisation tubes containing lysis buffer and immediately homogenise for 3 × 20 seconds at 5000 rpm.
Centrifuge lysates at 16000 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer supernatants to new Eppendorf tubes.
Incubate supernatants in a bench top shaker at 1400 rpm for 1 hour in the dark at room temperature.
Determine protein concentration of samples using bicinchoninic acid (BCA) assay or equivalent.
Store samples in the freezer at -80 °C until further processing.
Thaw samples by incubating on a bench-top shaker at room temperature until homogenously mixed.
Combine volumes equivalent to 150 µg of protein from heavy and light labelled samples for SICyLIA analysis using label-swap replication.
Transfer additional volumes equivalent to 150 µg of protein from all samples for dimethyl labelling, keeping them separate.
Bring the total volume of all samples to 300 μl by adding ammonium bicarbonate.
Add DTT to all samples to a final concentration of 71 mM.
Incubate in a bench-top shaker at 1000 rpm for 1 hour at room temperature or 4 °C.
Bring the volume to 650 µl by adding ammonium bicarbonate.
Add N-ethylmaleimide (NEM) to all samples to a final concentration of 90 mM.
Incubate in a bench-top shaker at 1000 rpm for 1 hour at room temperature.
Add TCA to all samples to a final concentration of 25% w/v to precipitate proteins.
Incubate in a bench-top shaker at 300 rpm for 15 minutes at 4 °C.
Centrifuge samples at 16000 g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Carefully remove supernatants and add 1 ml of TCA (10% stock solution) to protein pellets.
Incubate in a bench top shaker at 300 rpm for 15 min at 4 °C.
Centrifuge samples at 16000 g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Wash pellets with water until pH = 7.0 (typically 4-5 washes required).
After last wash, centrifuge samples at 16000 g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Remove supernatants and re-suspend protein pellets in 50 µl urea buffer (8 M stock solution in water).
Incubate in a bench top shaker at 1000 rpm for 15 min at room temperature.
Add 150 µl Ambic and vortex samples.
Add Lys-C (ratio 1:33 enzyme:protein) and incubate in a bench top shaker at 1000 rpm for 1 hour at room temperature.
Bring volume to 500 µl with Ambic (pH 7.0) and vortex samples.
Add Trypsin (ratio 1:25 enzyme:protein) and incubate overnight in a bench top shaker at 1000 rpm at room temperature.
Next morning, acidify samples with trifluoroacetic acid (TFA, 50% stock solution in water) to a final concentration of 5%.
Store forward/reverse mixed SICyLIA samples at -80°C until fractionation.
Wash SepPak columns with 100% acetonitrile, 2 x 1 ml.
Equilibrate the columns with RP buffer A, 4 x 1 ml.
Load samples onto their respective columns.
Wash the columns using RP buffer A, 2 x 1 ml.
Label peptides with light and heavy formaldehyde/cyanoborohydride solutions, using 5 x 1 ml each.
Wash the columns using RP buffer A, 2 x 1 ml.
Elute and collect labelled samples using 500 µl RP buffer B.
Further elute and collect labelled samples using 500 µl acetonitrile with 2.5% TFA.
Mix heavy and light dimethylated samples according to label-swap replication approach.
Reduce all sample volumes to 300 µl using vacuum centrifugation to remove ACN and TFA.
Bring the volume up to 500 µl per sample using HPLC solvent A.
Equilibrate the C18 column using 4% HPLC solvent B.
Inject 500 μl samples manually through a Rheodyne valve onto the RP-HPLC column.
Apply a two-step gradient at a flow-rate of 200 µl/min (from 4–27% B in 36 min, then from 27–48% B in 8 min).
Wash the column for 5 minutes at 80% solvent B.
Re-equilibrate the column for 10 minutes using the initial gradient conditions.
Monitor the column eluate at 220 and 280 nm.
Collect fractions from 9 to 54 minutes for 90 seconds per vial (300 µl).
Pool the first 4 and the last 5 fractions, resulting in a total of 21 fractions.
Dry the fractions to completion using vacuum centrifugation.
Store dried fractions at -80°C until analysis.
Reconstitute the dried fractionated tryptic digests in 10 μl of MS solvent A (water, 0.1% formic acid).
Separate samples by nanoscale C18 reverse-phase liquid chromatography using an EASY-nLC II 1200 (Thermo Scientific).
Elute using a binary gradient with MS solvent A (2% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid in water) and MS solvent B (80% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid in water) at a flow rate of 300 nl/min.
Use different gradients for three sets of fractions: F1-7, F8-15, and F16-21.
For F1-7, start with 2% MS solvent B, increase to 20% after 20 minutes, then to 39% after another 7 minutes.
For F8-14, start with 4% MS solvent B, increase to 23% after 20 minutes, then to 43% after another 7 minutes.
For F15-21, start with 6% MS solvent B, increase to 28% after 20 minutes, then to 48% after another 7 minutes.
Follow all gradients by a washing step (100% B) for 10 minutes.
Re-equilibrate the system with 5% B for 5 minutes.
Load samples with 8 µl of MS solvent A into a 20 cm fused silica emitter packed in-house with ReproSil-Pur C18-AQ, 1.9 μm resin.
Keep the packed emitter at 35 °C using a column oven integrated into the nanoelectrospray ion source.
Elute peptides are electrosprayed into the mass spectrometer using a nanoelectrospray ion source.
Use an Active Background Ion Reduction Device to decrease air contaminants signal level.
Specify methionine oxidation and N-terminal acetylation as variable modifications.
Set peptide, protein, and site false discovery rate (FDR) to 1%.

Set modification by light and heavy iodoacetamide on cysteine residues (carbamidomethylation) as label type modification in Andromeda configuration with composition sets HNOCx(2)Hx(2) for heavy and H3NOC2 for light label.
For dimethylated samples, set DimethLys0/Nter0 and DimethLys8/Nter8 as light and heavy labels, respectively.
Process both data sets (iodoacetamide heavy/light and dimethyl heavy/light) at the same time in MaxQuant using different parameters by defining these with the Parameter Groups option.
Import the proteinGroups.txt file into Perseus.
Filter rows based on categorical column “only identified by site”. Remove matching rows with value “+”, reduce matrix.
Filter rows based on categorical column “Reverse”. Remove matching rows with value “+”, reduce matrix.
Filter rows based on categorical column "Potential contaminant".
Remove matching rows with value "+".
Reduce matrix.
Remove empty columns.
Transform "1/(x)" the columns "Ratio H/L normalized" of the dimethyl-labelled reverse replicates.
Rename columns to reflect the format "wild-type over knock-out".
Export matrix.
Import peptides.txt and pre-processed proteinGroups.txt files into Perseus.
Match "id" in peptides.txt with "Peptide IDs" in proteinGroups.txt file.
Import the pre-processed "Ratio H/L normalized" columns of the dimethyl-labelled replicates.
Filter rows based on categorical column "Reverse".
Remove matching rows with value "+".
Reduce matrix.
Filter rows based on categorical column "Potential contaminant".
Remove matching rows with value "+".
Reduce matrix.
Filter rows based on categorical column "Unique (Groups)".
Remove matching rows with value "no".
Reduce matrix.
Filter rows based on numerical/main column where x > 0.
Remove empty columns.
Transform “1/(x)” for the columns “Ratio H/L normalized” of iodoacetamide-labelled reverse replicates, excluding already transformed protein ratio values.
Rename columns to reflect transformation applied.
Divide matrix access “Columns” by “Median”.
Combine main columns using Operation “x/y” to divide peptide ratio values by parent protein ratio values.
Rename columns to reflect normalization applied.
Categorically annotate rows to create Group1 including normalised peptide oxidation ratios for all replicates of each experimental condition.
Average groups, grouping “Group1”, with Average type “Mean”, keeping original data and adding “Standard deviation”.
Average groups using the median type and keep original data.
Add standard deviation to the results for each group.
Rename newly created columns for Mean, Mean SD, Median, and Median SD.
Change column types from Numerical to Main for the newly created columns.
Combine main columns using Operation “\(x/y) ==*== 100” with “x = Standard deviation of the peptide oxidation ratios” and “y = Mean of the peptide oxidation ratios” to calculate the CV%.
Rename columns to reflect the calculated CV%.
Calculate the median, inter-quartile range (IQR), first quartile (Q1), and third quartile (Q3) for the CV% column.
Calculate the cut-off for outlier values using the formula 1.5 × IQR + Q3.
Filter rows based on numerical/main column with x = “CV%” to exclude outliers beyond the calculated cut-off value.
Transform “log2(x)” the normalised peptide oxidation ratios.
Transform “Intensity” values.
Create Group1 to include normalised log2 peptide oxidation ratios for all replicate experiments.
Average groups in Group1 using median type averaging, keep original data, and add standard deviation.
Rename newly created columns for the log2 Median and log2 SD.
Change column type of newly created columns from “Numerical” to “Main”.
Identify peptides with significant positive and negative ratio value changes using Benjamini-Hochberg FDR threshold at 0.05.
Estimate density for x: log2 Median peptide oxidation ratio, y: log2 Intensity.
